verdicts.trueWording: one well written specific sentence is worth more than a page
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched with a browser UA (HTTP 200). Sentence sits in the details-vs-specifics paragraph of the Swan Hollow Intrigue review, prefaced by the picture/thousand-words comparison; 'of details' closes it. Every limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: It is terse, meaning it doesn't get in the way
verdicts.note: Same paragraph, defining Specificity against detail; the sentence continues about scanning an adventure and not pausing mid-game. Claim's 'the page' is the page of an adventure being scanned, and the DM is the reader throughout the paragraph.

verdicts.trueWording: It communicates exactly the vibe the DM should be going for.
verdicts.note: Closing sentence of the details-vs-specifics paragraph, immediately after the one-sentence/page-of-details line. Quotation word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: That (dubious) in parens tells us a lot.
verdicts.note: Next paragraph, on the Quack selling a (dubious) potion of healing. The page calls the table 'a wandering traveller table for one of the inns' rather than 'random-encounter table'; that is a naming difference, the entry is a rolled table entry and the parenthetical adjective limb is exact.

verdicts.trueWording: quick adjectives/adverbs used to describe NPCs hit so well
verdicts.note: Same paragraph; the contrast limb is the following sentence, where a long section of italics read-aloud per NPC meant to convey personality is said to fail. Both limbs on the page.
Stands as its own sentence inside the paragraph on long bouts of exposition and irrelevant detail, so the claim's framing as a verdict on exposition is the page's own context.

verdicts.trueWording: a mediocre at best prose poem in the form of
verdicts.note: Post is '7 Maxims of the OSR', section III 'Role Playing not Roll Playing', final sentence of the fruitful-voids paragraph: when such voids are everywhere one has no game, but that prose poem, shaped as an instruction manual or gazetteer. 'Made entirely of' maps to the page's 'when they are everywhere'. Byline renders via script, but Gus L answers as blog author throughout the comments.

Quotation is exact: Bryce quotes room 28 'Lower Hydra Nest' from Nikoline's Lions of Tell Arn Part 2 and does hold the writing up as the model ('That IS the goal of good writing'). But the entry he quotes is not verbless throughout - after the two noun phrases it runs a ledge line and then a finite-verb clause about water and blood dripping from above, and the ledge line is spatial rather than sensory. The neighbouring model rooms he praises open with finite verbs too (room 29's detritus thickens).
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'a string of verbless sensory noun phrases' - the same quoted room 28 entry ends in a finite-verb clause (water and blood dripping from above) and includes a non-sensory ledge/exit line

verdicts.trueWording: he usually wrote a 1-line note for each room
verdicts.note: Opening paragraph of the post (the tag archive renders the article in full). Page frames it as Gygax's first dungeon under Castle Greyhawk, notes shared with co-DM Rob Kuntz. Claim's limbs hold.

verdicts.trueWording: Gary's longer descriptions set the pattern for virtually every adventure
verdicts.note: Section 'Gary Gygax sets the standard'; the preceding sentences name G1 Steading of the Hill Giant Chief (1978) and generous descriptions for every location, so the G1 limb is on the page. Quoted sentence closes with 'to follow'.

verdicts.trueWording: ideas that spring to mind first will steer toward the obvious
verdicts.note: Section 'Longer descriptions'. The preceding sentence supplies the first limb: longer descriptions free DMs from needing to invent details at the table. The quoted clause continues about the most familiar and blandest ideas.

verdicts.trueWording: encourages authors to write something even when they have little to add
verdicts.note: Section 'Longer descriptions', on the padded taxidermist's-bedroom entry. Noting the wording gap honestly: the page says 'encourages' and 'little to add' where the claim says 'makes' and 'nothing to add'; the very next sentence carries the stronger form, saying the format makes authors feel obligated to describe an empty closet's shelves and pegs, so both limbs are supported in substance.

verdicts.trueWording: An avalanche of description does more than squander page count.
verdicts.note: Section 'Matching description to a location's purpose'; the next sentence (with a typo in the original) says it buries great details that might actually enter play, and the Victor Wachter example follows. Both limbs on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: The length of descriptions should match the way players will engage
verdicts.note: Section 'The ideal dungeon description'; sentence ends 'a location', followed by the widow's-salon versus Tomb of Horrors contrast. Claim's paraphrase matches.

verdicts.trueWording: the first thing a typical DM would imagine at the table
verdicts.note: Section 'The ideal dungeon description', final paragraph: if your kitchen description reads that way, you may as well rely on the typical imagination - which is the cutting test the claim describes.
